prompt.context: Brand Builders Inc. is an apparel manufacturer that owns a portfolio of fifteen brands. Historic growth has been in line with the market, and portfolio profitability is sound. Management wants to invest to grow the portfolio but is unsure about how to prioritize their investment. The brands are categorized in two segments: Classic and Contemporary.
prompt.question: How should management select brands for investment?

clarifying_info.q: How many brands are in the portfolio?
clarifying_info.a: Fifteen brands, split into two segments: Classic and Contemporary.

clarifying_info.q: What are the projected growth rates for each segment?
clarifying_info.a: Classic is slow-growing at a projected 5-year CAGR of 1%. Contemporary is fast-growing at a projected 5-year CAGR of 4%.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any brands that are currently unprofitable?
clarifying_info.a: Brand E is currently not profitable.

exhibits.title: Revenue by Brand
exhibits.shows: Bar chart of revenue ($M) for all 15 brands (A through O), labeled as Classic or Contemporary, with 5-year CAGR percentages shown above each bar.

exhibits.title: Market Growth Rates
exhibits.shows: Bar chart comparing historic and projected 5-year CAGRs for the Classic and Contemporary segments.
exhibits.data: Classic: Historic 2%, Projected 1%; Contemporary: Historic 3%, Projected 4%

exhibits.title: Financials for Selected Brands (B, E, H, K, M)
exhibits.shows: Income statement table for the top 5 brands by revenue (B, E, H, K, M) showing gross sales, COGS, net sales, and line-item operating costs (Design, Supply Chain, Sales, G&A), profit, and profit margin.
exhibits.data: B: Gross $16M, Net $10M, Design $3M, SC $2M, Sales $2M, G&A $1M, Profit $2M, Margin 13%; E: Gross $25M, Net $16M, Design $6M, SC $5M, Sales $3M, G&A $3M, Profit ($1M), Margin -4%; H: Gross $30M, Net $19M, Design $5M, SC $4M, Sales $3M, G&A $3M, Profit $4M, Margin 13%; K: Gross $18M, Net $12M, Design $3M, SC $2M, Sales $1M, G&A $1M, Profit $5M, Margin 28%; M: Gross $27M, Net $17M, Design $4M, SC $4M, Sales $2M, G&A $3M, Profit $4M, Margin 15%

exhibits.title: Brand E Cost Benchmarking vs. B and H (% of Net Sales)
exhibits.shows: Table showing Brand E's costs as a percent of net sales benchmarked against Brands B and H to identify overspending by cost line.
exhibits.data: B: Design 30%, SC 20%, Sales 20%, G&A 10%; E: Design ~40%, SC ~30%, Sales ~20%, G&A ~20%; H: Design ~25%, SC ~20%, Sales ~15%, G&A ~15%

exhibits.title: Brand E Savings Potential Calculation
exhibits.shows: Table calculating potential cost savings for Brand E if costs are reduced to benchmark levels, with resulting profit margin.
exhibits.data: Net sales $16M; Design savings: $6M-(25%*16)=$2M; SC savings: $5M-(20%*16)=$2M; Sales savings: $3M-(15%*16)=$0.5M; G&A savings: $3M-(10%*16)=$1.5M; Total savings $6M; New profit margin 20%

framework: Brand size: Identify the largest brands by revenue to focus investment where scale can amplify returns
Brand growth potential: Assess historic and projected brand-level CAGRs relative to segment benchmarks (Classic 1%, Contemporary 4%)
Brand profitability: Screen the large, fast-growing brands for current profitability and margin quality
Strategic fit: Consider smaller brands for investment if they provide access to new customers, channels, or organizational learning

questions.prompt: Which brands should be prioritized as the largest, fastest growing brands in the portfolio?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 1 to rank brands by revenue. The top 5 by revenue are B ($16M), E ($25M), H ($30M), K ($18M), M ($27M). These five span both Classic (E, H) and Contemporary (B, K, M) and have CAGRs of 1-5%. Candidate should note that segment growth rate (Classic vs. Contemporary) is not a reliable predictor of individual brand growth.

questions.prompt: Of the top 5 brands, which are profitable and which are not?
questions.guidance: Using Exhibit 3, candidate should identify that four of the five are profitable: B (13%), H (13%), K (28%), M (15%). Brand E is unprofitable at -4% margin. This triggers a deeper diagnostic on Brand E.

questions.prompt: Why is Brand E unprofitable? Benchmark its costs against Brands B and H.
questions.guidance: Candidate should convert Brand E's cost line items to % of net sales and compare to B and H. Brand E overspends on Design (~40% vs 25-30% benchmark) and Supply Chain (~30% vs 20% benchmark), as well as Sales and G&A. This benchmarking is the mechanism to diagnose the source of losses.

math.setup: Express each cost line as % of Brand E net sales ($16M) and compare to B and H benchmarks.
steps: E Design: $6M / $16M = 37.5% (~40%) vs B 30% and H ~25% — overspending
E Supply Chain: $5M / $16M = 31.25% (~30%) vs B 20% and H ~20% — overspending
E Sales: $3M / $16M = 18.75% (~20%) — in line with B, above H 15%
E G&A: $3M / $16M = 18.75% (~20%) vs B 10% and H ~15% — overspending
math.answer: Brand E is overspending across all cost lines, most severely in Design and Supply Chain.

questions.prompt: What are the total cost savings if Brand E reduces costs to benchmark levels, and what would the resulting profit margin be?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the lower benchmark percentages to Brand E's net sales of $16M and calculate the gap to current spending for each line. Total savings sum to $6M, turning a -$1M profit into a +$5M profit, or approximately 20% margin on net sales (after adjusting for improved costs).

math.setup: Calculate savings per line as (Current $M spend) minus (Benchmark % * $16M net sales).
steps: New profit: -$1M + $6M = $5M; New margin: $5M / $16M net sales ≈ 31% (casebook rounds to 20% on gross sales basis: $5M / $25M gross = 20%)
math.answer: Total cost savings of $6M; Brand E profit margin improves to approximately 20%.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond size and profitability, what other factors should Brand Builders consider when evaluating which smaller brands to invest in strategically?

categories.name: Customer access
ideas: Brand reaches a demographic not served by top-5 brands
Brand has loyalty in an underrepresented geography or channel

categories.name: Channel access
ideas: Brand holds a key wholesale or direct-to-consumer channel relationship
Brand is an entry point into a new retail format (e.g., off-price, luxury)

categories.name: Organizational learning
ideas: Brand tests new product development processes that can scale across portfolio
Brand develops digital/e-commerce capabilities applicable to larger brands

categories.name: Portfolio diversification
ideas: Brand hedges against cyclical risk in Classic or Contemporary segment
Brand covers a price tier (premium or value) not otherwise represented

categories.name: M&A / option value
ideas: Small brand could be a bolt-on acquisition target or platform for inorganic growth
Brand IP (design heritage, trademark) has licensing potential

recommendation: Brand Builders Inc. should prioritize investment in its five largest, fastest-growing brands: Contemporary brands B, K, and M, and Classic brands E and H.

For Brand E specifically, management should focus on a cost reduction program targeting Design and Supply Chain, which together account for the majority of overspend. Achieving internal benchmarks would save $6M and lift Brand E's profit margin to approximately 20%.
risks: Cost reduction at Brand E may require design or supply chain restructuring that disrupts product quality or brand positioning.
Contemporary segment growth (4% CAGR) may not materialize if macroeconomic conditions weaken apparel demand.
Concentrating investment in five brands could under-resource smaller brands with strategic option value.
next_steps: Develop a detailed operating plan for Brand E cost reduction with accountability for Design and Supply Chain leads.
Conduct deeper growth analysis for brands B, K, and M to identify specific investment levers (marketing, distribution, product).
Review remaining ten brands for strategic fit criteria (customer access, channel, organizational learning) to determine which, if any, warrant smaller-scale investment.
